subject: ACME bastion: private FQDN assertion & ACME proxy provisioning
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@harvestpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: partner.ops@edgebridge.io
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: private bastion for *.harvestpay.internal + cert flow

Hey Vivek,

Quick summary: HarvestPay is spinning up a private Redwood deployment inside our prod VPC. We need a pattern for asserting customer-owned private FQDNs (e.g., api.redwood.harvestpay.internal) and a recommended TLS termination approach that satisfies our netsec and internal audit constraints.

Constraints:
- No public DNS delegation (split-horizon only).
- Customer will run their own private ACME endpoint behind an internal bastion (not accessible from internet).
- All traffic must present mTLS to internal services and Redwood must be able to validate host certs.
- Audit requires proof of CSR origin and rotation schedule.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood accept CSRs produced by our internal ACME server and proxy key material through a bastion?
2) What does ownership assertion look like for a private-only FQDN?
3) Any recommended ingress proxy patterns (sidecar, central edge, or hybrid) to preserve end-to-end client identity?

I've attached a short requirements doc and a rough diagram. Alyssa

(attachment: harvestpay-acme-requirements.pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@harvestpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: private bastion for *.harvestpay.internal + cert flow

Thanks Alyssa — appreciate the level of detail. High-level answers up front: yes, we can support CSRs from a customer-run ACME behind a bastion, and we recommend a small set of ownership proofs + a proxy pattern that keeps TLS termination explicit in the VPC.

Two core options we typically recommend:
- Edge proxy (central) inside customer VPC: handles TLS termination and mTLS to Redwood runtime, supports SNI mapping and OCSP stapling, easier to audit.
- Sidecar integration (per-node): preserves original client certs end-to-end but increases operational complexity and token costs for scaling.

For private ownership assertion we use a two-part proof: (A) CSR signed by the customer's internal CA/ACME and (B) short-lived token proof returned by Redwood to a customer-run bastion endpoint (we call this the bastion assertion flow). That way, the private DNS owner proves control without exposing DNS to public resolution.

Marissa — can you draft the checklist we should ask HarvestPay to provide (CSR format, CA metadata, bastion reachable endpoint for assertion token)? Kimberly — please confirm whether we need to require OCSP responder access or if stapling + signed CRS is sufficient for audit.

Vivek

(attachment: acme-csr-templates.zip)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@harvestpay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: private bastion for *.harvestpay.internal + cert flow

Alyssa — putting the checklist below. I also sketched a hybrid proxy approach (central ingress + optional sidecars for high-security paths) and attached a sample proxy config.

Ownership & CSR checklist (minimal):
- Signed CSR bundle: PEM CSR + issuing CA cert chain (PEM).
- CSR metadata file: subjectAltNames, requested lifetimes, key algo (RSA2048/ECP256 preferred).
- Bastion assertion endpoint: curlable internal endpoint (https://bastion-internal.harvestpay.local/assert) that can accept a Redwood POST containing a nonce. Bastion must return the nonce signed with the private key corresponding to the ACME account key.
- Proof of rotation policy: doc indicating rotation cadence and last rotation timestamps.
- Optional: internal OCSP responder URI if HarvestPay wants us to check revocation in real time.

Hybrid proxy recommendation:
- Deploy a central TLS edge proxy (LB/HAProxy/nginx/Envoy) in the customer's private subnet to terminate client TLS and validate client mTLS.
- Edge proxy performs SNI -> backend mapping and forwards validated identity to Redwood runtime via mTLS using a customer-provided leaf cert.
- For services requiring strict client identity (payments, secrets access), use a local sidecar that terminates the client and forwards an identity token internally to the service.

Security notes:
- Do not hand Redwood private keys. Redwood prefers customers to retain private keys; we accept signed CSRs and deploy the certs on our side if requested, or we can accept the cert + key via an HSM integration when contractually allowed.
- For audit: keep the bastion assertion logs (nonce exchanges) and CSR timestamps in your internal audit store; Redwood will replicate assertion receipts to the tenant audit logs.

Next steps: Alyssa, if you can provide the CSR bundle and a reachable assertion endpoint in a staging VPC, we can run a dry-run and produce an assertion receipt. Timeline estimate: 3 business days after we receive the CSR + assertion endpoint and access to a staging bastion ACL.

(attachment: proxy-proposal-v1.yaml)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@harvestpay.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding: private bastion for *.harvestpay.internal + cert flow

Thanks all — this is helpful. A few clarifications/questions inline: 

> Bastion assertion endpoint: curlable internal endpoint (https://bastion-internal.harvestpay.local/assert) that can accept a Redwood POST containing a nonce. Bastion must return the nonce signed with the private key corresponding to the ACME account key.

We can expose that endpoint inside our staging VPC. The ACME account key is currently stored in our bastion HSM — signing there is doable but requires an API shim. Can Redwood support verifying a JWT signed by our bastion HSM instead of a raw RSA signature? It would simplify our shim.

> Do not hand Redwood private keys. Redwood prefers customers to retain private keys; we accept signed CSRs and deploy the certs on our side if requested, or we can accept the cert + key via an HSM integration when contractually allowed.

We'd prefer to keep keys inside our HSM. Our ask: can Redwood accept the signed cert (PEM) and trust chain, and configure the edge proxy with that cert while keys never leave our HSM? What changes in the onboarding checklist if keys remain in HSM?

Action items from HarvestPay:
- We'll provide CSR bundle + staging assertion endpoint by EOD Friday.
- We'll confirm HSM signing capability and whether we can emit a JWKS endpoint for the bastion.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute runbook call next week to walk through the nonce exchange and the staging dry-run.

—Alyssa
